description: ROS-responsive delivery of exosomes (e.g., MSC-exo, sEVs, plant-derived exosomes) in chronic diabetic wounds remains unexplored — all current exosome-loaded smart hydrogels (PMID30662554, PMID38286650, PMID39891270, PMID40391025, PMID41355885, PMID42165000) use non-responsive or pH/temperature/light-responsive matrices, but none leverage ROS-triggered release despite high wound ROS levels driving inflammation and impairing healing.
rationale: ROS is a dominant, persistent feature of chronic diabetic wounds (>10× physiological levels), yet no study couples exosome payload with ROS-cleavable linkers (e.g., thioketal, boronic ester, arylboronate) for on-demand, inflammation-activated release. This represents a missed opportunity for spatiotemporal immunomodulation precisely where and when it’s needed.
novelty_query: ((exosome OR "extracellular vesicle" OR sEV) AND (hydrogel OR scaffold) AND (ROS-responsive OR "reactive oxygen species responsive") AND (diabet* wound OR chronic wound))

description: No reported smart敷料 combines biofilm-disrupting enzymatic activity (e.g., DNase I, dispersin B, alginate lyase) with real-time, enzyme-responsive (MMP/NE/elastase) release — while MMP/enzyme-responsive systems exist (PMID35857459, PMID37420287), they deliver antimicrobials or growth factors, not enzymes targeting biofilm matrix components.
rationale: Biofilms in chronic wounds are structurally reinforced by eDNA, polysaccharides, and proteins; yet current enzyme-responsive hydrogels release effectors that act *on cells*, not *on the biofilm scaffold*. Co-loading and enzyme-triggered release of biofilm-degrading enzymes would enable autonomous, microenvironment-activated biofilm clearance — a critical unmet need for MRSA/P. aeruginosa-infected chronic wounds.
novelty_query: ("biofilm enzyme" OR "DNase I" OR "dispersin B" OR "alginate lyase") AND (hydrogel) AND ("MMP-responsive" OR "elastase-responsive" OR "neutrophil elastase-responsive") AND (wound)

description: Despite extensive use of copper (Cu²⁺, CuONPs, Cu-MOFs) in diabetic wound dressings (PMID36582352, PMID38784443, PMID39629118, PMID41709316, PMID41981667), no system integrates Cu²⁺ with *glucose-responsive release* — all Cu-delivery systems are either passive, pH/NIR/thermo-triggered, or lack glucose-sensing capability, missing the opportunity to couple hyperglycemia-driven demand with therapeutic supply.
rationale: Chronic hyperglycemia directly impairs angiogenesis and macrophage function; glucose-responsive Cu²⁺ release would allow dose escalation precisely under high-glucose conditions (e.g., via phenylboronate–cis-diol binding), enhancing pro-angiogenic and antimicrobial effects only when pathologically relevant — a feedback-controlled therapeutic strategy absent in current literature.
novelty_query: (copper OR "Cu2+" OR "copper oxide") AND (hydrogel) AND ("glucose-responsive" OR "glucose-sensitive" OR "phenylboronate") AND (wound OR "diabetic wound")

description: All published thermosensitive hydrogels for chronic wounds (PMID40755899, PMID40243670, PMID38379700, PMID36811095, PMID39280109) are tested *only in rodent models* — none have advanced to large-animal (e.g., porcine or diabetic rabbit) validation, representing a critical translational gap for injectable/thermo-gelling systems intended for clinical deployment.
rationale: Thermosensitive gels rely on precise sol–gel transition kinetics near body temperature; porcine skin thickness, perfusion, and wound contraction dynamics differ markedly from rodents. Absence of large-animal data prevents assessment of clinical feasibility (e.g., retention time, mechanical integrity under movement, dosing accuracy), stalling regulatory pathway development.
novelty_query: ("thermosensitive" OR "temperature-responsive" OR "thermo-gelling") AND hydrogel AND (wound) AND (porcine OR pig OR rabbit OR "large animal")

description: No intelligent敷料 reported to date targets *Enterococcus faecium* or *Acinetobacter baumannii* biofilms — while MRSA and P. aeruginosa are widely addressed (PMID35857459, PMID39280109, PMID41909502), these two ESKAPE pathogens dominate polymicrobial chronic wounds in ICU and long-term care settings and exhibit extreme biofilm resilience, yet remain neglected in smart hydrogel design.
rationale: E. faecium forms ultra-dense, vancomycin-tolerant biofilms on necrotic tissue; A. baumannii produces copious extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) resistant to conventional antimicrobials. Their absence from smart敷料 studies reflects a clinically dangerous oversight — especially given rising multidrug resistance and association with non-healing surgical and pressure ulcers.
novelty_query: ("Enterococcus faecium" OR "Acinetobacter baumannii") AND (biofilm) AND (hydrogel OR dressing) AND (smart OR "stimuli-responsive" OR "intelligent")

description: Although light-responsive oxygen-generating systems exist (PMID32440554, PMID38030563, PMID39210966), none integrate *real-time, closed-loop oxygen sensing* (e.g., phosphorescent O₂ probes) with light-triggered photosynthetic activation — all are open-loop (fixed irradiation), failing to adapt to dynamic hypoxia fluctuations in chronic wounds.
rationale: Chronic wound hypoxia is heterogeneous and dynamic (e.g., fluctuates with perfusion, infection burden, dressing occlusion); open-loop light delivery risks over-oxygenation (ROS burst) or under-oxygenation (inefficacy). A feedback-integrated system would maximize safety and efficacy — a key engineering gap preventing clinical translation of photobiomodulatory hydrogels.
novelty_query: (oxygen OR "O2 generation") AND (hydrogel) AND (photosynthetic OR chloroplast OR "thylakoid") AND ("oxygen sensor" OR "phosphorescent probe" OR "closed-loop") AND (wound)

description: No dual-enzyme-responsive (MMP-9 + NE) hydrogel has been developed for chronic wounds — while single-enzyme responsiveness appears (PMID35857459: MMP-2/9; PMID37420287: pH/enzyme dual), neutrophil elastase (NE) is equally elevated in chronic wounds and synergizes with MMPs to degrade ECM and growth factors; co-targeting both remains unreported.
rationale: MMP-9 and NE are co-upregulated, interdependent proteases in diabetic wounds; NE activates pro-MMP-9, and both cleave collagen, fibronectin, and IGF-1. A hydrogel degradable *only* upon co-presence of both enzymes would provide unprecedented specificity for pathological (not physiological) remodeling zones — enabling precision delivery while avoiding premature degradation.
novelty_query: ("MMP-9" OR "matrix metalloproteinase-9") AND ("neutrophil elastase" OR NE) AND (hydrogel) AND (responsive OR "dual-responsive") AND (wound)

description: Despite strong rationale for combining ROS-scavenging (e.g., NAC, curcumin) with NO-donor therapy to resolve inflammation and promote angiogenesis, no ROS-responsive hydrogel co-delivers both modalities — existing ROS-responsive systems deliver only one (PMID31083588: edaravone; PMID38797862: Mg-GA MOFs; PMID41909502: DFO-Mn-ZIF), and NO donors appear only in NIR-responsive systems (PMID40810663).
rationale: ROS and NO crosstalk critically regulates macrophage polarization (M1→M2) and endothelial function; simultaneous, co-localized, ROS-triggered release of both scavenger and NO donor would create a self-limiting anti-inflammatory–pro-angiogenic cascade — a synergistic mechanism validated in vitro but never engineered into an intelligent敷料 for chronic wounds.
novelty_query: (NAC OR curcumin OR "N-acetylcysteine") AND (NO OR "nitric oxide" OR "NO donor") AND (hydrogel) AND ("ROS-responsive" OR "reactive oxygen species responsive") AND (wound)

description: All current exosome-loaded hydrogels (PMID30662554, PMID38286650, PMID39891270, PMID40391025, etc.) use *mammalian or plant-derived exosomes*, but none employ *engineered bacterial extracellular vesicles (BEVs)* — which offer superior scalability, endotoxin-controllable production, and inherent TLR2/4 adjuvant activity ideal for immune reprogramming in chronic wounds.
rationale: BEVs can be genetically programmed to carry wound-healing miRNAs, antimicrobial peptides, or anti-fibrotic cytokines, and their gram-negative origin provides built-in immunostimulatory signals to reverse chronic immune paralysis — a uniquely tunable, GMP-compatible platform absent from current smart敷料 literature.
novelty_query: ("bacterial extracellular vesicle" OR BEV OR "outer membrane vesicle") AND (hydrogel) AND (wound OR "diabetic wound")

description: No smart敷料 reported uses *hypoxia-responsive* release (e.g., azobenzene, nitroimidazole, or HIF-1α-binding peptide motifs) — while pH/ROS/enzyme/light/temperature responses are well-represented (PMID35857459, PMID31083588, PMID38797862, etc.), hypoxia is a defining, persistent feature of chronic wounds (~1–5 mmHg vs. normal 40 mmHg) and remains untargeted as a trigger.
rationale: Hypoxia drives HIF-1α stabilization, which upregulates VEGF, SDF-1, and glycolytic enzymes — yet no hydrogel exploits this master regulator as a release trigger. Hypoxia-responsive systems would enable *endogenous biomarker-guided* delivery of angiogenic factors or metabolic modulators only within truly ischemic wound niches — maximizing therapeutic index and minimizing off-target effects.
novelty_query: (hypoxia-responsive OR "HIF-responsive" OR "nitroimidazole" OR azobenzene) AND hydrogel AND (wound OR "chronic wound")

description: While multiple hydrogels load growth factors (EGF, IGF-1, bFGF, PDGF-BB — PMID40599340, PMID36234898, PMID40319298, PMID39816695), none implement *sequential, multi-stage release* (e.g., early anti-inflammatory → mid-proliferative → late-maturation) using orthogonal stimuli (e.g., pH → ROS → MMP) — all reported systems use single- or dual-trigger release without temporal programming.
rationale: Chronic wound healing failure stems from dysregulated phase progression (e.g., prolonged inflammation, stalled proliferation). A tri-stimuli-responsive hydrogel releasing IL-4/IL-10 first (pH-triggered), then EGF/bFGF (ROS-triggered), then decorin/TGF-β3 (MMP-triggered) would recapitulate physiological healing chronology — a systems-level design gap in current biomaterials.
novelty_query: ("sequential release" OR "staged release" OR "temporal release") AND (hydrogel) AND (growth factor OR cytokine) AND (wound) AND (pH OR ROS OR "MMP" OR enzyme)

description: No intelligent敷料 integrates *real-time, on-site detection* (e.g., colorimetric/fluorometric readout) of wound biomarkers (pH, ROS, MMP-9, NE) with therapeutic response — all responsive systems (PMID36714604, PMID38797862, PMID41909502) are 'blind' actuators; diagnostic feedback is entirely absent from the material interface.
rationale: Clinical decision-making for chronic wounds relies on subjective assessment; integrating low-cost, visible biomarker sensing (e.g., ROS-sensitive dye + therapeutic release) would enable patient- or nurse-guided dressing changes and adaptive therapy — bridging the critical gap between smart materials and point-of-care diagnostics. No such theranostic hydrogel exists for chronic wounds.
novelty_query: (theranostic OR "diagnostic hydrogel" OR "sensing hydrogel") AND (wound) AND (pH OR ROS OR "MMP-9" OR "neutrophil elastase")
